question_text: The Civil Service Commission issued a MANDATORY directive. What does 'mandatory' mean?

hint_ladder.title: Orient: Meaning ng Mandatory
hint_ladder.text: Isipin mo, "mandatory" = "must." Sa exam, kapag may directive na mandatory, ibig sabihin ay required, hindi optional.

hint_ladder.title: Rule: Mandate = Command
hint_ladder.text: Mandatory galing sa salitang "mandate." Ang mandate ay utos. Kapag utos, walang palag—kailangan gawin. Kaya mandatory means required.

hint_ladder.title: Apply: Eliminate Choices
hint_ladder.text: Tingnan ang choices: "Optional" means may choice. "Suggested" at "Advisory" ay payo lang, hindi sapilitan. Ang tamang sagot ay "Required."

hint_ladder.title: Nearly Give Away: Barangay Scenario
hint_ladder.text: Sa barangay assembly, kapag mandatory ang attendance, hindi ka puwedeng umiwas. Required talaga. I-match mo: mandatory = required. Sagot ay B.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you thought 'mandatory' means voluntary, but it actually means the opposite—required.

B.text: Correct. 'Mandatory' means required, compulsory, or obligatory—something you must do because an authority commands it.

C.text: You might have chosen C because 'suggested' sounds similar, but a suggestion is just a recommendation, not a mandatory order.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'advisory' seems official, but advisory is non-binding advice, not a required action.

deconstruct_text:
Sa barangay assembly, mandatory ang attendance. Ibig sabihin, walang choice—kailangan pumunta, kundi may penalty. 'Yan ang ibig sabihin ng 'mandatory' sa CSC directive: requirement, hindi suggestion.

Now, the options: 'Optional' is kabaliktaran—may choice ka. 'Suggested' and 'Advisory' are recommendations, not forced. Only 'Required' means 'must-do.' So 'mandatory' = required.
